headline: N-able takes remote access platform offline after zero-days disclosed
summary: N-able took its hosted and self-hosted remote access platform offline and urged customers to shut down servers after a security researcher publicly disclosed dozens of zero-day vulnerabilities, some allowing full system takeover.

claims.statement: N-able took its remote-access platform offline and urged customers to shut down servers after a researcher disclosed dozens of zero-days.

sources.quote: N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published

N-able has taken its hosted N-central environments offline and urged on-premises customers to shut down their servers after a security researcher publicly disclosed more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities, including exploits that could let attackers take over vulnerable systems.
N-able takes its remote access service offline after researcher publishes dozens of zero-day bugs
The remote access giant also urged its self-hosted customers to take down their own servers amid a "critical security incident," fearing the possibility of cyberattacks.
